arb.why: AT1 blockade reduces vasoconstriction and aldosterone effects.

ace.why: ACE inhibition reduces angiotensin II and aldosterone.

dhp.pair: Dihydropyridine CCB: relaxes arterial smooth muscle
dhp.why: Vascular L-type calcium-channel blockade produces arterial vasodilation.

beta1.pair: Beta1 blocker: reduces cardiac adrenergic stimulation
beta1.why: Cardiac beta1 blockade reduces heart rate and contractile workload.

nonselective_beta.pair: Nonselective beta blocker: blocks beta1 and beta2 receptors
nonselective_beta.why: Beta1 and beta2 blockade explains cardiac effects and bronchospasm risk.

alpha_beta.pair: Alpha/beta blocker: reduces vascular and cardiac adrenergic effects
alpha_beta.why: Labetalol combines alpha1 with beta1/beta2 blockade.

verapamil.pair: Non-dihydropyridine CCB: slows AV-nodal calcium-dependent conduction
verapamil.why: Verapamil acts in the AV node and myocardium.

hydralazine.pair: Direct vasodilator: relaxes arteriolar smooth muscle
hydralazine.why: Hydralazine reduces arterial resistance through direct smooth-muscle relaxation.

arb_dhp.pair: ARB plus dihydropyridine CCB: receptor blockade and arterial dilation
arb_dhp.why: The combination contains valsartan and amlodipine.

arb_thiazide.pair: ARB plus thiazide: receptor blockade and sodium loss
arb_thiazide.why: The combination contains valsartan and hydrochlorothiazide.

ics_laba.pair: ICS plus LABA: airway anti-inflammatory and bronchodilator effects
ics_laba.why: Budesonide suppresses airway inflammation; formoterol stimulates beta2 receptors.

tramadol.pair: Opioid/monoamine analgesic: mu agonism and reuptake inhibition
tramadol.why: Tramadol combines weak mu activity with serotonin/norepinephrine reuptake effects.

opioid.why: Mu-receptor agonism provides analgesia and can depress consciousness and breathing.

paracetamol.pair: Non-opioid analgesic: predominantly central analgesic/antipyretic action
paracetamol.why: Paracetamol treats pain and fever without the usual NSAID platelet/GI effects.

nsaid.pair: NSAID: inhibits cyclooxygenase and reduces prostaglandins
nsaid.why: Reduced prostaglandins explain analgesia, anti-inflammatory effects, and important adverse effects.

gabapentin.pair: Gabapentinoid: binds the alpha-2-delta calcium-channel subunit
gabapentin.why: This modulates excitatory neurotransmitter release; it is not a direct GABA agonist.

sodium_anticonvulsant.pair: Anticonvulsant: stabilizes inactivated voltage-gated sodium channels
sodium_anticonvulsant.why: Carbamazepine and phenytoin limit repetitive neuronal firing through sodium-channel effects.

tca.why: Additional antimuscarinic, antihistamine, and sodium-channel actions explain important adverse effects.

benzodiazepine.why: Enhanced inhibitory GABA activity produces anticonvulsant and sedative effects.

ketamine.why: NMDA antagonism underlies dissociative anesthesia; airway complications remain possible.

beta_lactam.pair: Beta-lactam: inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis through PBPs
beta_lactam.why: Penicillin-binding-protein inhibition disrupts bacterial cell-wall construction.

glycopeptide.why: Vancomycin inhibits cell-wall synthesis by binding precursor termini.

fluoroquinolone.pair: Fluoroquinolone: inhibits bacterial DNA gyrase/topoisomerase IV
fluoroquinolone.why: These effects impair bacterial DNA replication.

aminoglycoside.pair: Aminoglycoside: disrupts protein synthesis at the 30S subunit
aminoglycoside.why: Gentamicin acts on the bacterial 30S ribosomal subunit.

linezolid.pair: Oxazolidinone: inhibits protein synthesis at the 50S subunit
linezolid.why: Linezolid interferes with bacterial protein synthesis; its class distinguishes it from other 50S agents.

clindamycin.pair: Lincosamide: inhibits protein synthesis at the 50S subunit
clindamycin.why: Clindamycin is a lincosamide, distinct from oxazolidinones despite a shared broad ribosomal target.

metronidazole.pair: Nitroimidazole: forms metabolites that damage microbial DNA
metronidazole.why: Susceptible anaerobic organisms and protozoa are targeted by reactive metabolites.

nystatin.pair: Polyene antifungal: disrupts sterol-containing fungal membranes
nystatin.why: Nystatin binds fungal membrane sterols; oral local therapy does not treat systemic infection.

warfarin.pair: Vitamin-K antagonist: reduces vitamin-K-dependent factor synthesis
warfarin.why: VKORC1 inhibition reduces regeneration of vitamin K and synthesis of functional clotting factors.

lmwh.pair: LMWH: enhances antithrombin activity, predominantly against Xa
lmwh.why: LMWH activity is predominantly anti-Xa; different products are not dose-for-dose interchangeable.

ufh.pair: Unfractionated heparin: enhances antithrombin inhibition of IIa/Xa
ufh.why: UFH accelerates inhibition of thrombin and activated factor X.

aspirin.why: Reduced thromboxane A2 synthesis impairs platelet aggregation.

clopidogrel.pair: Antiplatelet: irreversibly inhibits platelet P2Y12 receptors
clopidogrel.why: Its active metabolite inhibits ADP-mediated platelet activation.

alteplase.pair: Fibrinolytic: activates plasminogen to break down fibrin
alteplase.why: Alteplase promotes fibrin breakdown; it is distinct from preventing new coagulation.

nitrate.why: Nitrates relax vascular smooth muscle and reduce cardiac workload.

norepinephrine.why: Norepinephrine supports vascular tone and pressure, with some beta1 activity.

dobutamine.why: Dobutamine primarily supports cardiac pumping and output.

dopamine.pair: Catecholamine: dose-dependent dopaminergic and adrenergic effects
dopamine.why: Dopamine can provide selected hemodynamic support; effects depend on the regimen.

atropine.pair: Antimuscarinic: reduces vagal slowing of the heart
atropine.why: Muscarinic blockade removes parasympathetic slowing rather than directly stimulating beta1 receptors.

adenosine.pair: A1-receptor agonist: briefly blocks AV-nodal conduction
adenosine.why: Its very short action requires rapid delivery when used in the indicated rhythm pathway.

propafenone.pair: Class Ic antiarrhythmic: blocks fast sodium channels
propafenone.why: Propafenone slows conduction and is unsuitable in important structural/conduction disease contexts.

lidocaine.pair: Class Ib antiarrhythmic: blocks fast sodium channels
lidocaine.why: IV cardiac lidocaine is distinct from local-anesthetic preparations with additives.

amiodarone.pair: Predominantly class III agent: multiple channel/adrenergic effects
amiodarone.why: Amiodarone affects several cardiac ion channels and adrenergic signaling.

digoxin.pair: Cardiac glycoside: inhibits Na/K ATPase and increases vagal tone
digoxin.why: It increases contractile calcium availability while slowing AV-nodal conduction.

loop.pair: Loop diuretic: inhibits Na-K-2Cl transport in the ascending loop
loop.why: Furosemide promotes salt and water loss, reducing congestion.

spironolactone.why: Aldosterone antagonism reduces sodium retention and potassium loss.

sglt2.pair: SGLT2 inhibitor: increases renal glucose and sodium excretion
sglt2.why: Dapagliflozin acts on renal sodium-glucose cotransport rather than supplying insulin.

insulin.pair: Insulin: activates receptors to promote glucose uptake
insulin.why: Insulin increases glucose uptake and suppresses hepatic glucose production.

ppi.pair: Proton-pump inhibitor: suppresses gastric H/K ATPase
ppi.why: Blocking the final gastric acid-secretory pump reduces acid production.

lactulose.pair: Osmotic laxative: retains water in the colon
lactulose.why: A nonabsorbable disaccharide promotes stool passage through colonic osmotic effects.

metoclopramide.why: Dopamine blockade contributes to antiemesis and extrapyramidal adverse effects.

antispasmodic.pair: Peripheral antimuscarinic: reduces GI/GU smooth-muscle spasm
antispasmodic.why: Hyoscine butylbromide treats spasm without resolving every underlying cause of abdominal pain.

promethazine.pair: First-generation H1 antagonist: sedating antihistamine/antiemetic effects
promethazine.why: Promethazine also has anticholinergic effects and can add to opioid-related sedation.

betahistine.why: Histaminergic effects are used for vertigo; it is not a primary cardiac emergency drug.

saba.pair: Short-acting beta2 agonist: relaxes bronchial smooth muscle
saba.why: Salbutamol relieves bronchospasm; repeated doses may lower potassium.

aminophylline.pair: Methylxanthine: bronchodilation with a narrow therapeutic index
aminophylline.why: Theophylline-related PDE/adenosine effects contribute to bronchodilation and toxicity.

steroid.why: Corticosteroids have anti-inflammatory effects with glucose, infection, and suppression risks.

bicarbonate.why: Bicarbonate changes acid-base balance and is reserved for selected indications.

dextrose.pair: Hypertonic IV glucose: supplies rapidly available glucose
dextrose.why: Concentrated dextrose can correct severe hypoglycemia but can injure tissue if extravasated.

calcium.pair: IV calcium salt: supports calcium and cardiac membrane stability
calcium.why: In hyperkalemic ECG toxicity, calcium stabilizes myocardium without removing potassium.

magnesium.pair: Electrolyte: modulates membrane stability and repolarization
magnesium.why: Magnesium has indication-specific replacement and antiarrhythmic roles.

statin.why: Reduced cholesterol synthesis lowers LDL and contributes to cardiovascular prevention.

multivitamin.pair: Vitamin/mineral supplement: effects depend on the ingredients
multivitamin.why: Composition varies, so a single universal mechanism or dose cannot be assumed.

cefazolin.pair: First-generation cephalosporin: inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
cefazolin.why: Cefazolin is a first-generation cephalosporin beta-lactam acting through PBPs.

meropenem.pair: Carbapenem beta-lactam: inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
meropenem.why: Meropenem is a carbapenem beta-lactam acting through PBPs.

ceftazidime.pair: Third-generation cephalosporin: inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis
ceftazidime.why: Ceftazidime is a third-generation cephalosporin beta-lactam acting through PBPs.

ibd2-meropenem.use: Treatment of serious susceptible bacterial infection

trolley-29.use: Treatment of nausea with a prokinetic role

ibd2-epanutin-phenytoin.use: Prevention or treatment of selected seizures

ibd2-vancomycin.use: Systemic treatment of serious susceptible Gram-positive infection

ibd2-fortum-ceftazidime.use: Treatment of susceptible serious Gram-negative infection

ibd2-scobutyl-hyoscine-butylbromide.use: Relief of GI or GU smooth-muscle spasm

ccu-isosorbide-dinitrate.use: Relief of angina using the prescribed nitrate formulation

ccu-nadroparin.use: Prescribed anticoagulation for selected thromboembolic indications

ccu-enoxaparin.use: Prescribed anticoagulation in ACS or thromboembolic disease

ccu-clopidogrel.use: Antiplatelet treatment after ACS or coronary stenting

ccu-propranolol.use: Selected rate, BP, or angina treatment

ccu-verapamil.use: Selected supraventricular rate control or angina treatment

ccu-enalapril.use: Selected chronic hypertension or heart-failure treatment

ccu-furosemide.use: Relief of congestion and fluid overload

ccu-dapagliflozin.use: Selected chronic diabetes, HF, or kidney-disease treatment

ccu-norepinephrine.use: Pressure support in severe hypotension or shock

ccu-dobutamine.use: Pump support in selected low-output states

ccu-pantoprazole.use: Prescribed acid suppression or GI protection

ccu-omeprazole.use: Prescribed acid suppression or GI protection

ccu-metronidazole.use: Treatment of susceptible anaerobic or protozoal infection

ccu-linezolid.use: Treatment of serious resistant Gram-positive infection

ccu-propafenone.use: Rhythm control in carefully selected arrhythmia patients

ccu-symbicort.use: Ongoing prescribed asthma or COPD treatment

ccu-adenosine.use: Protocol-directed treatment of selected regular SVT

ccu-labetalol.use: Controlled lowering of severe BP when indicated

ccu-ketamine.use: Procedural sedation or anesthesia under trained supervision

ccu-pethidine.use: Prescribed analgesia in selected severe pain

ccu-morphine.use: Prescribed treatment of selected severe pain or distress

trolley-spironolactone.use: Selected chronic HFrEF, hypertension, or aldosterone-related retention

trolley-dextrose50.use: IV treatment of severe symptomatic hypoglycemia

trolley-hydrocortisone.use: Adrenal crisis or selected severe inflammatory states

trolley-diazepam.use: Selected seizure, agitation, or sedation treatment

trolley-calcium-gluconate.use: Selected symptomatic hypocalcemia or hyperkalemic ECG toxicity

trolley-aminophylline.use: Selected bronchodilation under an authorized regimen

ibd2-amitriptyline.use: Depressive illness or prescribed off-label neuropathic-pain treatment

verified-alteplase-v35.use: Indication-specific emergency thrombolysis in eligible patients
